title: Annotatio IV §.II open: Cosinus mentions John 6 and Paul as mode-commentaries
pass_a_gloss: §. II. Most opportunely the Most Learned Bishop here injects mention both of Christ’s discourse on eating His flesh and drinking His blood in John 6, and of Paul’s discourse on the communion of the Eucharistic bread and cup with the body and blood of Christ.
pass_b_english: §.II: Cosinus (Most Learned Bishop) aptly brings in two discourses here.
John 6 — eating Christ’s flesh and drinking His blood; and Paul — communion of Eucharistic bread and cup with Christ’s body and blood.
source_text: §. II. Oportunè admodum Doctiss. Episcopus cùm Sermonis Christi de manducanda carne sua, & bibendo sanguine suo Joh. 6. tum Sermonis Paulini, de panis & poculi Eucharisticorum communione cum corpore & sanguine Christi, mentionem hôc locô injicit.
